definition.en: The practice in which services are given to the agent as small command-line tools, each with a README that the agent reads only when it needs the tool, instead of MCP servers. [1][2][3][4]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой сервисы отдают агенту как небольшие утилиты командной строки, у каждой свой README, который агент читает только когда утилита нужна, вместо MCP-серверов. [1][2][3][4]

sources.quote: All my stateless tools (like Jira, AWS, GitHub) have been migrated to simple CLIs.
sources.author: Shrivu Shankar
sources.work: How I Use Every Claude Code Feature

sources.quote: The alternative is simple: build CLI tools with README files. The agent reads the README when it needs the tool, pays the token cost only when necessary (progressive disclosure), and can use bash to invoke the tool.
sources.author: Mario Zechner
sources.work: What I learned building an opinionated and minimal coding agent

sources.quote: One of the reasons we strongly lean towards CLI and bash is because it allows easy composition of calls, and because the model also learns how the file system works when it’s trained.
sources.author: Armin Ronacher
sources.work: What is Codemode

sources.quote: The simplest form is text, so by default, whatever I wanna build, it starts as CLI. Agents can call it directly and verify output - closing the loop.
sources.author: Peter Steinberger
sources.work: Shipping at Inference-Speed

definition.en: The practice in which a team runs the same agent tasks as evals with and without a change to instruction files or documentation, and keeps the change only after several runs show an improvement. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой команда прогоняет одни и те же задачи агента как evals с изменением в файлах инструкций или документации и без него и оставляет изменение, только если несколько прогонов показали улучшение. [1]

sources.quote: To test these concerns, we created a set of evaluations that measured agent performance within our current setup against a branch without root-level documentation files.
sources.author: Addie Beach, Rui Martins Lacerda
sources.work: How we built data-driven AI Golden Paths at Datadog

title.en: Check that the instruction file is loaded

definition.en: The practice in which the developer checks which instruction file the agent tool actually reads, for example with a marker word, before relying on it. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик проверяет, какой файл инструкций агент на самом деле читает, например по контрольному слову, прежде чем на него полагаться. [1][2]

sources.quote: Check which filename your harness actually honours, because an ignored instruction file is silent.
sources.author: Systima
sources.work: Claude Code Is Way More Token-Hungry Than OpenCode. We Measured Exactly How Much

sources.quote: I made an empty directory that holds only an AGENTS.md with a canary word in it, and asked claude -p for the word.
sources.author: Przemek
sources.work: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when telemetry is on

definition.en: The practice in which a prompt or workflow that the developer keeps repeating is saved as a skill or command file, checked into git and run by name. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой промпт или порядок действий, который разработчик повторяет снова и снова, сохраняется как скилл или команда, кладётся в git и запускается по имени. [1]

sources.quote: If you do something more than once a day, turn it into a skill. Anything you repeat is a skill waiting to be written.
sources.author: Arpan Patel
sources.work: Beyond the Prompt: Claude Code

title.en: Repository knowledge as the system of record

definition.en: The practice in which decisions, plans, conventions and other context are kept as versioned files in the repository instead of chats, documents and people's heads, so that agents can read them. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой решения, планы, соглашения и прочий контекст хранятся как версионируемые файлы в репозитории, а не в чатах, документах и головах людей, чтобы агенты могли их прочитать. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: We learned that we needed to push more and more context into the repo over time.
sources.author: Ryan Lopopolo
sources.work: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world

sources.quote: PRDs, ADRs, UI Specs, and Design Docs live in their own directories (docs/prd/, docs/adr/, docs/ui-spec/, docs/design/) and are intended to be committed.
sources.author: shinpr
sources.work: GitHub - shinpr/claude-code-workflows: Development workflows for Claude Code that keep broad exploration focused on the outcome you approved.

sources.quote: We also maintained architecture decision records (ADR) that captured every significant structural choice, so the AI followed decisions the team had already made, rather than guessing.
sources.author: Shashank Mishra
sources.work: AI-assisted migration: Critical lessons from the modernization frontlines

definition.en: The practice in which a long agent session is summarized at a milestone or near the context limit, with instructions on what the summary keeps, and work continues in a new context from the summary. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой длинную сессию агента сжимают в краткое изложение на рубеже работы или у предела контекста, с указанием, что сохранить, и работа продолжается в новом контексте с этого изложения. [1]

sources.quote: Compact at milestones. After you finish a logical chunk, run /compact Preserve the decisions made, files changed, and test commands.
sources.author: Arpan Patel
sources.work: Beyond the Prompt: Claude Code

definition.en: The practice in which several agents or models work on the same problem at the same time, each with its own approach, and the developer compares the results. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой несколько агентов или моделей одновременно работают над одной задачей, каждый своим подходом, а разработчик сравнивает результаты. [1][2]

sources.quote: We've found that having multiple models attempt the same problem and picking the best result significantly improves the final output, especially for harder tasks.
sources.author: Lee Robinson
sources.work: Cursor agent best practices

sources.quote: Instead of dividing the work, have agents compete on it. Spawn N agents that each attempt the same task using different approaches.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar and Sid Bidasaria
sources.work: A harness for every task: dynamic workflows in Claude Code

definition.en: The practice in which the application can be started separately in each git worktree, so that every agent runs and checks its own instance. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой приложение запускается отдельно в каждом git worktree, и каждый агент запускает и проверяет свой экземпляр. [1][2]

sources.quote: For example, we made the app bootable per git worktree, so Codex could launch and drive one instance per change.
sources.author: Ryan Lopopolo
sources.work: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world

sources.quote: On this app I share one stack and give each worktree its own ports, database names, and resource names.
sources.author: Ally Piechowski
sources.work: Your Setup Script Should Support Git Worktrees

definition.en: The practice in which agents search parts of an application for one category of vulnerability, a separate verifier agent proves each finding with a test in the application's own test suite, and findings arrive as pull requests. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агенты ищут в частях приложения уязвимости одной категории, отдельный агент-проверяющий доказывает каждую находку тестом в наборе тестов самого приложения, а находки приходят как pull request. [1]

sources.quote: It enables authors to easily create category-specific bug hunting agents, which then run safely, provide a test oracle, and open PRs for findings.
sources.author: Zack Deveau
sources.work: Building an agentic harness that outlasts the model (2026)

title.en: Vertical slices in agent work plans

definition.en: The practice in which the agent's work plan for a feature is cut into vertical slices that cross backend and frontend, so that integration is exercised before the end of the work. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой план работы агента над фичей режут на вертикальные срезы через бэкенд и фронтенд, чтобы интеграция проверялась до конца работы. [1][2]

sources.quote: Backend and frontend design stay separate, a consistency check covers the boundary between them, and the work plan uses vertical slices so integration is exercised before the end.
sources.author: shinpr
sources.work: GitHub - shinpr/claude-code-workflows: Development workflows for Claude Code that keep broad exploration focused on the outcome you approved.

sources.quote: And in most cases, I'll send off a model to do 1-3 slices at a time, and review the code as I go. It's a lot easier to resteer early on, whether it's the internals or the actual functionality, than to end up on the other side of 2k+ lines of code with no idea what's broken.
sources.author: Dex
sources.work: advanced-context-engineering-for-coding-agents/wsff.md at main

definition.en: The practice in which contributors state in the pull request, commit message or post whether and how a model or agent produced the content. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой участники указывают в pull request, коммите или сообщении, создавали ли содержимое модель или агент и как. [1][2]

sources.quote: Contributors should note tool usage in their pull request description, commit message, or wherever authorship is normally indicated for the work.
sources.author: rnk
sources.work: [RFC] LLVM AI tool policy: human in the loop

sources.quote: You must disclose LLM-generated content. You can choose to not post LLM content, or you can choose to post it and disclose its origin.
sources.author: Jynn Nelson
sources.work: rust-lang/rust is adopting an LLM policy

definition.en: The practice in which a project requires contributors to read and review all generated code or text, and to be able to explain it, before they ask maintainers for review. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой проект требует от авторов вкладов прочитать и проверить весь сгенерированный код или текст и уметь его объяснить, прежде чем просить ревью у мейнтейнеров. [1]

sources.quote: Contributors must read and review all LLM-generated code or text before they ask other project members to review it.
sources.author: rnk
sources.work: [RFC] LLVM AI tool policy: human in the loop

title.ru: Свои слова в общении в проекте

definition.en: The practice in which a project requires issues, pull request descriptions, comments and replies to review to be written in the contributor's own words, not pasted model output. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой проект требует, чтобы issues, описания pull request, комментарии и ответы на ревью были написаны своими словами автора, а не вставленным выводом модели. [1][2]

sources.quote: Passing maintainer feedback to an LLM doesn’t help anyone grow, and does not sustain our community.
sources.author: rnk
sources.work: [RFC] LLVM AI tool policy: human in the loop

sources.quote: In short, if you are posting any of those things, the output must be your own words, explanation, description, etc., not a verbatim dump of an LLM's output.
sources.author: Jellyfin project
sources.work: LLM/"AI" Policies

title.en: Agents in project spaces only with approval
title.ru: Агенты в пространствах проекта только с одобрения

definition.en: The practice in which an agent may comment on or act in shared project spaces only after people approve it or explicitly invoke it. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент может комментировать или действовать в общих пространствах проекта только после одобрения людьми или по явному вызову. [1][2]

sources.quote: An important implication of this policy is that it bans agents that take action in our digital spaces without human approval, such as the GitHub @claude agent.
sources.author: rnk
sources.work: [RFC] LLVM AI tool policy: human in the loop

sources.quote: This skill requires explicit invocation because it can comment, label, or close another person's contribution.
sources.author: Wirasm
sources.work: GitHub - Wirasm/prp: Prompts, workflows and more for agentic engineering

definition.en: The practice in which maintainers who judge a generated contribution to cost more review time than it is worth reply with a standard request, label it, and stop engaging or close it. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой мейнтейнеры, решив, что сгенерированный вклад отнимает на ревью больше времени, чем стоит, отвечают стандартной просьбой, ставят метку и прекращают обсуждение или закрывают вклад. [1][2]

sources.quote: Other reviewers should use the label to prioritize their review time.
sources.author: rnk
sources.work: [RFC] LLVM AI tool policy: human in the loop

sources.quote: You are allowed to close PRs that don't follow the policy, no questions asked. Please point the author to #llm-mentoring at the same time.
sources.author: Jynn Nelson
sources.work: rust-lang/rust is adopting an LLM policy

definition.en: The practice in which a project does not accept contributions that include content generated, in part or in full, by language models or similar systems. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой проект не принимает вклады, содержащие материал, созданный целиком или частично языковыми моделями или похожими системами. [1][2]

sources.quote: Contributions in the OpenJDK Community must not include content generated, in part or in full, by large language models, diffusion models, or similar deep-learning systems.
sources.author: OpenJDK Governing Board
sources.work: OpenJDK Interim Policy on Generative AI

sources.quote: This patch thus defines a policy that the QEMU project will currently not accept contributions where use of AI code generators is either known, or suspected.
sources.author: Daniel P. Berrangé
sources.work: [PATCH v2 3/3] docs: define policy forbidding use of AI code generators

definition.en: The practice in which a project lets contributors use language models to answer questions, analyze, check and review their work, but not to create the content they submit. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой проект разрешает участникам использовать языковые модели, чтобы отвечать на вопросы, анализировать, проверять и ревьюить свою работу, но не создавать то, что они присылают. [1][2]

sources.quote: It's fine to use LLMs to answer questions, analyze, distill, refine, check, suggest, review. But not to create.
sources.author: Jynn Nelson
sources.work: rust-lang/rust is adopting an LLM policy

sources.quote: Contributors in the OpenJDK Community may use generative AI tools privately to help comprehend, debug, and review OpenJDK code and other content, and to do research related to OpenJDK Projects, so long as they do not contribute content generated by such tools.
sources.author: OpenJDK Governing Board
sources.work: OpenJDK Interim Policy on Generative AI

definition.en: The practice in which shared agent controls used by many teams, such as skills, commands and root-level instruction files, have an owning team or guild. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой у общих настроек агентов, которыми пользуются многие команды (навыки, команды, файлы инструкций в корне), есть команда или гильдия-владелец. [1]

sources.quote: On the other hand, more complex controls like skills, commands, or root-level documentation may be owned by entire teams or guilds.
sources.author: Addie Beach, Rui Martins Lacerda
sources.work: How we built data-driven AI Golden Paths at Datadog

title.ru: Вопросы об агентах в разборе инцидентов

definition.en: The practice in which a team's regular incident retrospective adds two questions: whether agent-written code contributed to the incident, and whether the larger volume of change strained review, testing, rollout or observability. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой в регулярный разбор инцидентов команды добавляют два вопроса: повлиял ли на инцидент код, написанный агентом, и не перегрузил ли возросший объём изменений ревью, тестирование, выкатку или наблюдаемость. [1]

sources.quote: During our AI ramp-up, we began asking two additional questions: Did AI-authored code directly contribute to the incident? And did the increased volume of change put additional pressure on review, testing, rollout, or observability?
sources.author: Tyson Singer
sources.work: AI Changed How Spotify Builds. What We Learned (and Fixed) About Quality at Higher Velocity

title.en: Extra approval for agent pull requests
title.ru: Повышенная планка для pull request агента

definition.en: The practice in which pull requests started by an agent or generated by a model must clear a higher bar than other pull requests, such as more human approvals or required tests. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой pull request, начатые агентом или созданные моделью, должны пройти более высокую планку, чем остальные: больше одобрений людей или обязательные тесты. [1][2]

sources.quote: We’ve settled on 2 human approvals for any AI-initiated PR for now, but it is kind of a weird paradigm shift (for me at least) when it’s no longer a human making something for another human to review.
sources.author: Shrivu Shankar
sources.work: How I Use Every Claude Code Feature

sources.quote: LLM PRs are required to have tests, full stop, regardless of how hard that is, as well as various other restrictions;
sources.author: Jynn Nelson
sources.work: rust-lang/rust is adopting an LLM policy

definition.en: The practice in which an engineer now and then solves a problem without an agent, even one the agent could solve, to keep their own skills. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой инженер время от времени решает задачу без агента, даже если агент бы с ней справился, чтобы сохранить свои навыки. [1]

sources.quote: To combat this, some engineers deliberately practice without AI: "Every once in a while, even if I know that Claude can nail a problem, I will not ask it to. It helps me keep myself sharp."
sources.author: Saffron Huang, Bryan Seethor, Esin Durmus, Kunal Handa, Miles McCain, Michael Stern, Deep Ganguli
sources.work: How AI is transforming work at Anthropic

definition.en: The practice in which an interview gives the candidate a few hours to build a working prototype with coding agents and tools of their choice. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой на собеседовании кандидату дают несколько часов, чтобы собрать работающий прототип с агентами и инструментами на свой выбор. [1][2]

sources.quote: After that, the candidate gets two hours to build a working prototype of the system they just designed using any AI model they want, and any frameworks.
sources.author: Applied Intuition
sources.work: Hiring engineers for the age of agents

sources.quote: The centerpiece of our on-site was a three-hour build session. Candidates chose from a short list of assigned prompts and were asked to design, build, and deploy a working prototype on DigitalOcean by the end of the session.
sources.author: DigitalOcean
sources.work: What We Learned Hiring 33 Engineers in Two Weeks

title.en: Assessing how a candidate directs agents
title.ru: Оценка того, как кандидат направляет агента

definition.en: The practice in which interviewers score how a candidate plans the work, steers the agent and checks what it produced. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой интервьюеры оценивают, как кандидат планирует работу, направляет агента и проверяет результат. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: Steering, not just prompting. Are you thinking about the how and why of the work, or just feeding the spec to an agent and hoping for the best?
sources.author: Elicit
sources.work: Engineering interviews in the era of agents - Elicit

sources.quote: Can they effectively direct and validate AI-generated work?
sources.author: Augment Code
sources.work: How we hire AI-native engineers now: our criteria

sources.quote: The candidates who really stand out use AI tools strategically and purposefully. They use AI to accelerate their development workflow while maintaining full ownership of the technical decisions.
sources.author: Karl Hörnlund
sources.work: AI Interview Success: An Interviewer's Inside Guide

title.en: Candidate's own agents in the interview

definition.en: The practice in which a candidate may use their own coding agents and tools during an interview, the same ones they would use at work. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой кандидат может пользоваться на собеседовании своими агентами и инструментами, теми же, что и на работе. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: The interviews where we want you to use AI tend to be deeper technical sessions. You’re on your own machine, using whatever tools you’re comfortable with.
sources.author: Elicit
sources.work: Engineering interviews in the era of agents - Elicit

sources.quote: We’re open to any type of tools, from none at all, to autocompletes, to full coding agents.
sources.author: Omnea
sources.work: Why we let candidates use AI in our programming interviews

sources.quote: We've piloted a new competency we called "AI-Assisted Coding" that replaces our traditional Computer Science Fundamentals screening for backend and frontend engineering roles.
sources.author: Simon Newton
sources.work: Yes, You Can Use AI in Our Interviews. In fact, we insist

title.en: Review of a draft change in the interview

definition.en: The practice in which a candidate reviews and improves a colleague's draft pull request in an unfamiliar codebase, with agents allowed. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой кандидат на собеседовании проверяет и дорабатывает черновой pull request коллеги в незнакомой кодовой базе, с агентами. [1]

sources.quote: Candidates are given a medium-sized codebase and a draft PR from a colleague that introduces a cross-cutting feature. Their job is to review and improve it — pulling down the code, inspecting the output, and iterating with coding agents to make it better.
sources.author: Sierra
sources.work: The AI-native interview

definition.en: The practice in which some interviews are deliberately held without agents, next to interviews where agents are expected. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой часть собеседований намеренно проводят без агентов, рядом с теми, где агенты ожидаются. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: There are some interviews where we explicitly ask candidates not to use AI.
sources.author: Elicit
sources.work: Engineering interviews in the era of agents - Elicit

sources.quote: Keep our technical phone screen as is. A 45-minute coding task with no AI.
sources.author: Applied Intuition
sources.work: Hiring engineers for the age of agents

sources.quote: This is all you–no AI assistance unless we indicate otherwise. We’re curious to see how you think through problems in real time.
sources.author: Anthropic
sources.work: Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage

title.en: Regular audit of the agent setup

definition.en: The practice in which, every few weeks, the developer audits the agent setup, including skills, plugins, instruction files and memory, with the tool's check command and reviews which parts still hold true. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик раз в несколько недель проверяет настройку агента, включая скиллы, плагины, файлы инструкций и память, командой проверки инструмента и пересматривает, что из этого ещё верно. [1]

sources.quote: And so I think there’s high value personally in, like maybe every couple of weeks, maybe at once a month even, just running doctor on your skills, on your setup, and auditing what you’re doing and seeing, okay, well, what still holds true?
sources.author: Addy Osmani
sources.work: Audit your Agent files

definition.en: The practice in which tests are kept as data files with the input, the expected output and the setup, read by a small test runner, so that agent changes to the tests are visible and can be blocked. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой тесты хранятся как файлы данных со входом, ожидаемым результатом и подготовкой, а читает их небольшой тестовый раннер, чтобы правки агента в тестах были видны и их можно было запретить. [1]

sources.quote: The tests are a contract that establishes what the code should do for us, and moving tests to data files, interpreted by a relatively smaller test runner, makes them easier to protect from unexpected manipulation by AI.
sources.author: Matteo Vaccari
sources.work: Tests as data

definition.en: The practice in which faults are injected into production code, by hand, by the agent or by a library in CI, to check that tests written by an agent break with a clear error message. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой в продакшен-код вносят намеренные ошибки, вручную, руками агента или библиотекой в CI, и проверяют, что тесты, написанные агентом, падают с понятным сообщением об ошибке. [1][2]

sources.quote: The first thing we can do is mutation testing: we inject intentional faults in production code, and see if any test breaks, and if it breaks, check that the error message is correct and informative.
sources.author: Matteo Vaccari
sources.work: Tests as data

sources.quote: I asked AI (in a clean new session — all of these steps were done in separate conversations to avoid context pollution) to review the code without looking at the tests, and to identify possible places where we can intentionally introduce a bug.
sources.author: Senko Rašić
sources.work: Improving AI-generated tests using mutation testing

definition.en: The practice in which test files and expected results that a task should not change are protected from the agent: made read-only, checked in CI for changes, or named in the agent's instructions as inputs to keep. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой файлы тестов и ожидаемые результаты, которые задача не должна менять, защищают от агента: делают доступными только для чтения, проверяют на изменения в CI или указывают в инструкциях агента как неизменяемые. [1][2]

sources.quote: Depending on the type of task, it’s possible to protect the files that we’re not expecting the AI to change, by making them read-only in a way that the agent cannot bypass, or by running a check in CI that verifies what files were changed depending on the type of task.
sources.author: Matteo Vaccari
sources.work: Tests as data

sources.quote: The agent was instructed to preserve those inputs and the skill’s verification helpers, investigate failures, and correct the implementation or execution setup rather than weaken the expectations.
sources.author: Naresh Jain
sources.work: Are Harnesses Worth the Cost?

definition.en: The practice in which, for medium- and high-risk pull requests, an agent guides the engineer through how the change affects the system, with understanding of the change, not approval, as the goal. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой для pull request среднего и высокого риска агент проводит инженера по тому, как изменение влияет на систему, и цель — понимание изменения, а не одобрение. [1]

sources.quote: We’ve been experimenting with a new process called Intent Review. For medium and high risk PRs, the agent guides the engineer through understanding how the change affects the system. The goal is comprehension, not approval.
sources.author: Vinay Perneti and Emma Webb
sources.work: The State of AI-Native Engineering 2026

origin.en: Named by Vinay Perneti and Emma Webb (Augment Code)
origin.ru: Название дали Винай Пернети и Эмма Уэбб (Augment Code)

definition.en: The practice in which agents read the codebase, issues, pull requests and discussion threads and write a knowledge base of unrecorded decisions and conventions, which other agents use when they work on the code. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агенты читают код, issues, pull request и обсуждения и пишут базу знаний о незаписанных решениях и соглашениях, которой другие агенты пользуются, когда работают с кодом. [1]

sources.quote: Agents that crawl the codebase, the issues, the PRs, the threads, and produce a knowledge base of the implicit decisions, the conventions, the why-we-did-it-this-way that nobody had time to document.
sources.author: .txt
sources.work: The bottleneck was never the code

title.ru: Управление агентом на самом узком уровне

definition.en: The practice in which a team corrects an agent behavior with the control of the smallest scope that still gives the wanted output: first interface and output contracts, then automated checks, then skills or commands, and root instruction files last. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой команда исправляет поведение агента средством самого узкого охвата, которое ещё даёт нужный результат: сначала контракты интерфейса и вывода, затем автоматические проверки, затем скиллы или команды и в последнюю очередь корневые файлы инструкций. [1]

sources.quote: At Datadog, we aim to use the control with the smallest scope that still gives us the output we want.
sources.author: Addie Beach, Rui Martins Lacerda
sources.work: How we built data-driven AI Golden Paths at Datadog

title.en: Volunteer-only review of model-written pull requests
title.ru: Ревью pull request от модели только добровольцами

definition.en: The practice in which a project assigns pull requests written with a language model only to reviewers who volunteer for them, and such a reviewer may ask the author to redo the change without generated code. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой проект отдаёт pull request, написанные с помощью языковой модели, только тем ревьюерам, кто вызвался их проверять, и такой ревьюер может попросить автора переделать изменение без сгенерированного кода. [1]

sources.quote: No one is required to review LLM PRs unless they volunteer.
sources.author: Jynn Nelson
sources.work: rust-lang/rust is adopting an LLM policy

definition.en: The practice in which each benchmark an agent optimizes also runs in CI as a guardrail whose threshold may only move in one direction, and benchmarks that are flaky or do not track the real metric are dropped. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой каждый бенчмарк, который оптимизирует агент, также работает в CI как ограничитель с порогом, который может сдвигаться только в одну сторону, а нестабильные или не отражающие реальную метрику бенчмарки убираются. [1][2]

sources.quote: Each one had two jobs: first, a metric Claude could move in the lab; second, a guardrail in CI with a number that could only ratchet down.
sources.author: Raymond Wang, Sam Attard, and Issac G.
sources.work: How we made claude.ai 3x faster in two weeks

sources.quote: If a benchmark was flaky, or if it didn’t actually correlate with user latency, we threw it out rather than let Claude climb the wrong hill.
sources.author: Raymond Wang, Sam Attard, and Issac G.
sources.work: How we made claude.ai 3x faster in two weeks

definition.en: The practice in which an agent is given a measured number to beat and repeatedly changes the code and re-measures until the number improves. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агенту дают измеряемое число, которое надо улучшить, и он раз за разом меняет код и перемеряет, пока число не улучшится. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: As soon as Claude had a number to beat, it could start optimizing.
sources.author: Raymond Wang, Sam Attard, and Issac G.
sources.work: How we made claude.ai 3x faster in two weeks

sources.quote: Agents yearn for tight feedback loops. They allow them to hill-climb to their heart's content.
sources.author: sankalp
sources.work: Auto-research with codex: How I achieved a 232x Faster Kernel over baseline with Codex in GPU Mode's qr_v2 problem

sources.quote: So we defined what healthy meant, instrumented the surface to answer it, and ran the whole change → measure → improve loop unattended.
sources.author: Alberto Gimeno
sources.work: Rendering huge pull requests in the GitHub Copilot app

definition.en: The practice in which several agents look for bugs in a change at the same time, a separate group of agents votes on each finding, and only findings with enough votes are posted. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой несколько агентов одновременно ищут ошибки в изменении, отдельная группа агентов голосует по каждой находке, и публикуются только находки, набравшие достаточно голосов. [1][2]

sources.quote: Several agents look for bugs at the same time. Then a separate group votes on each finding, and it only gets posted if enough of them agree it's real.
sources.author: Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang
sources.work: How the Claude Code team does code review

sources.quote: One of the most effective quality improvements we found early on was running multiple bug-finding passes in parallel and combining their results with majority voting. Each pass received a different ordering of the diff, which nudged the model toward different lines of reasoning.
sources.author: Jon Kaplan
sources.work: Building a better Bugbot

definition.en: A team rule in which every finding of the review agent must be fixed or resolved with a stated reason, and a pull request cannot merge while a bug or security finding is open. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Командное правило, при котором каждую находку агента-ревьюера нужно исправить или закрыть с указанием причины, а пул-реквест нельзя слить, пока открыта находка об ошибке или безопасности. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: Every finding has to be answered. You either fix it or resolve the thread with a reason.
sources.author: Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang
sources.work: How the Claude Code team does code review

sources.quote: A PR can't merge while any finding from the bug review or the security review is still open.
sources.author: Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang
sources.work: How the Claude Code team does code review

sources.quote: Every finding it raises becomes a discussion thread that has to be resolved — fixed, or explicitly dismissed with a reason — before the branch can merge.
sources.author: Christopher Olsen
sources.work: Putting an AI Reviewer in the Merge Gate

definition.en: A team rule in which the person who directed the agent counts as one of the required reviewers of its pull request, and an agent's approval never counts as a person's. [1][2]
definition.ru: Командное правило, при котором человек, направлявший агента, считается одним из обязательных ревьюеров его пул-реквеста, а одобрение агента никогда не засчитывается как одобрение человека. [1][2]

sources.quote: Whoever prompted the change is on the hook for it. On an agent-written PR, the person directing the agent counts as one of the required reviewers, the same as if they'd typed the code themselves.
sources.author: Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang
sources.work: How the Claude Code team does code review

sources.quote: An agent's approval never counts as a person's, either.
sources.author: Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang
sources.work: How the Claude Code team does code review

definition.en: A team rule in which a review approval covers one specific commit, and new commits the system cannot vouch for, such as an agent's push or a hand-resolved merge, require approval again. [1][2]
definition.ru: Командное правило, при котором одобрение ревью относится к одному конкретному коммиту, а новые коммиты, за которые система не ручается, например пуш агента или слияние, разрешённое вручную, требуют повторного одобрения. [1][2]

sources.quote: An approval covers one specific commit. If new commits land that the system can't vouch for, like an agent's push or a merge someone resolved by hand, the approval has to be given again.
sources.author: Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang
sources.work: How the Claude Code team does code review

sources.quote: A person may approve a particular revision. New code can change the basis for that decision.
sources.author: Maksym Kuzmitskyi
sources.work: A Review Belongs to a Commit

definition.en: The practice in which agents that read untrusted content, such as public issues or messages, are barred from high-privilege actions, and those actions are done by separate agents. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агентам, читающим недоверенный контент, например публичные задачи или сообщения, запрещены действия с высокими правами, а такие действия выполняют отдельные агенты. [1][2]

sources.quote: A useful pattern for triage workflows is quarantine. This involves barring the agents that read untrusted public content from taking high-privilege actions, which are instead done by the agents in charge of acting on the information.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar and Sid Bidasaria
sources.work: A harness for every task: dynamic workflows in Claude Code

sources.quote: The agent reads messages and issues that other people wrote, and that text can be interpreted as instructions. Limit what the agent could do if it followed them.
sources.author: Lance Martin and CJ Avilla
sources.work: Building effective agent automations

definition.en: The practice in which parallel agents take work from a shared list, and an agent claims a task, for example by writing a lock file, before working on it, so that no two agents take the same task. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой параллельные агенты берут работу из общего списка, и агент занимает задачу, например записывая файл-блокировку, прежде чем работать над ней, чтобы двое не взяли одно и то же. [1][2]

sources.quote: Claude takes a "lock" on a task by writing a text file to current_tasks/ (e.g., one agent might lock current_tasks/parse_if_statement.txt, while another locks current_tasks/codegen_function_definition.txt).
sources.author: Nicholas Carlini
sources.work: Building a C compiler with parallel Claudes

sources.quote: Subtasks: A to-do list where any agent can add a task and the first helper to claim it owns it.
sources.author: Barry Zhang, Tianyi Peng, Elle Najt, Keller Scholl, and Lance Martin
sources.work: Safely scaling multi-agent teams with Claude Fable 5.2

definition.en: The practice in which a harness runs the agent in a loop: when one task finishes, the next run starts, until a stop condition such as no new findings or no errors is met. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой обвязка запускает агента в цикле: когда одна задача закончена, начинается следующий прогон, пока не выполнено условие остановки, например нет новых находок или ошибок. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: To elicit sustained, autonomous progress, I built a harness that sticks Claude in a simple loop (if you’ve seen Ralph-loop, this should look familiar). When it finishes one task, it immediately picks up the next.
sources.author: Nicholas Carlini
sources.work: Building a C compiler with parallel Claudes

sources.quote: For tasks with an unknown amount of work, loop spawning agents until a stop condition is met (no new findings, or no more errors in the logs) instead of a fixed number of passes.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar and Sid Bidasaria
sources.work: A harness for every task: dynamic workflows in Claude Code

sources.quote: Ralph is a technique. In its purest form, Ralph is a Bash loop.
sources.author: Geoffrey Huntley
sources.work: Ralph Wiggum as a "software engineer"

definition.en: The practice in which test and CI output is kept short and fast for the agent: a few lines on screen, details written to a log file, progress printed rarely. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой вывод тестов и CI делается коротким и быстрым для агента: несколько строк на экране, подробности в лог-файле, прогресс печатается редко. [1][2]

sources.quote: The test harness should not print thousands of useless bytes. At most, it should print a few lines of output and log all important information to a file so Claude can find it when needed.
sources.author: Nicholas Carlini
sources.work: Building a C compiler with parallel Claudes

sources.quote: Two things have to be true for CI to function as part of an agent’s feedback loop. It has to be fast, and it has to be AI-legible.
sources.author: Liz Fong-Jones
sources.work: AI Amplifies Your Existing Practices: Lessons from Our Shift to an AI-First Strategy

definition.en: The practice in which the output of agent-written code is compared against an existing known-good implementation, which also narrows down which part of the agent's code is at fault. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой результат кода, написанного агентом, сравнивают с существующей заведомо верной реализацией, что также помогает найти, какая часть кода агента виновата. [1][2]

sources.quote: The fix was to use GCC as an online known-good compiler oracle to compare against. I wrote a new test harness that randomly compiled most of the kernel using GCC, and only the remaining files with Claude’s C Compiler.
sources.author: Nicholas Carlini
sources.work: Building a C compiler with parallel Claudes

sources.quote: Automated comparison tests validated behavioral parity between legacy endpoints and migrated APIs.
sources.author: Aditya Sharma and Mahesh Kharade
sources.work: Reimagining API modernization with deterministic AI-assisted engineering

definition.en: The practice in which a list of rules or claims is checked by separate verifier agents, one for each rule or claim. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой список правил или утверждений проверяют отдельные агенты-проверяющие, по одному на каждое правило или утверждение. [1][2]

sources.quote: If you have a particular set of rules that you find Claude misses or struggles with, even when put into the CLAUDE.mds, create a workflow with a list of rules that must be checked by verifier agents—one verifier per rule.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar and Sid Bidasaria
sources.work: A harness for every task: dynamic workflows in Claude Code

sources.quote: On the other hand, if you have a report where you want to check and source every factual claim that it references you may want to generate a workflow which has one agent identify all of the factual claims and then spin off a subagent to check each one in-detail.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar and Sid Bidasaria
sources.work: A harness for every task: dynamic workflows in Claude Code

definition.en: The practice in which several agents form hypotheses about a bug from separate, non-overlapping pieces of evidence, so that one early guess does not shape the whole investigation. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой несколько агентов строят гипотезы об ошибке по отдельным, непересекающимся частям данных, чтобы одна ранняя догадка не определяла всё расследование. [1]

sources.quote: A workflow can structurally prevent this by spinning up agents to generate hypotheses from disjoint evidence.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar and Sid Bidasaria
sources.work: A harness for every task: dynamic workflows in Claude Code

definition.en: The practice in which the agent writes plans, explanations and code reviews as HTML pages instead of Markdown documents. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент пишет планы, объяснения и разбор кода в виде HTML-страниц вместо документов Markdown. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: I’ve started preferring HTML as an output format instead of Markdown and increasingly see this pattern being applied by others on the Claude Code team.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar
sources.work: Using Claude Code: The unreasonable effectiveness of HTML

sources.quote: Use HTML to understand code that the agent has written, to review code, or to explain a PR to someone reviewing your code.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar
sources.work: Using Claude Code: The unreasonable effectiveness of HTML

sources.quote: I keep my agent planning and spec-driven development work in HTML.
sources.author: Nick Keuning
sources.work: Why I Use HTML for Planning and Spec-Driven Development

definition.en: The practice in which the agent builds a disposable interface for editing something by hand, and the interface ends with an export button that turns the edits into a prompt or a file. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент делает одноразовый интерфейс для ручного редактирования, и этот интерфейс завершается кнопкой экспорта, превращающей правки в промпт или файл. [1]

sources.quote: The trick is always to end with an export: a "copy as JSON" or "copy as prompt" button that turns whatever I did in the UI back into something I can paste into Claude Code or commit to a file.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar
sources.work: Using Claude Code: The unreasonable effectiveness of HTML

definition.en: The practice in which, before the agent writes code, the author walks the future pull request reviewer through the product and technical specs. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой до того, как агент напишет код, автор проходит продуктовую и техническую спецификацию с будущим ревьюером пул-реквеста. [1]

sources.quote: If you wanna save time during review, you pick the person who would review the PR, and run through the product/tech specs with them before you get to the coding part
sources.author: Dex
sources.work: advanced-context-engineering-for-coding-agents/wsff.md at main

definition.en: The practice in which agents log every attempted idea and its result, and later agent sessions read the log to see whether an idea was already tried. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агенты записывают каждую опробованную идею и её результат, а следующие сессии агентов читают журнал, чтобы понять, пробовали ли идею раньше. [1]

sources.quote: Logs serve as the evidence of the ideas that worked and didn't work. Future agent sessions could read the logs and quickly check if an idea had been tried or not.
sources.author: sankalp
sources.work: Auto-research with codex: How I achieved a 232x Faster Kernel over baseline with Codex in GPU Mode's qr_v2 problem

definition.en: The practice in which an agent puts its own changes behind feature flags for gradual rollout and reads the flag's results as feedback on whether the change does what it claimed. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент сам закрывает свои изменения флагами функций для постепенного выката и использует результаты флага как обратную связь о том, делает ли изменение заявленное. [1][2]

sources.quote: The new angle is that agents can be given the ability to gate their own changes for gradual rollout; the flag itself becomes the feedback signal for whether the change is doing what it claimed.
sources.author: Liz Fong-Jones
sources.work: AI Amplifies Your Existing Practices: Lessons from Our Shift to an AI-First Strategy

sources.quote: The first stage of our rollout process usually involves Claude managing canary traffic, monitoring for issues, and automatically ramping a given feature flag up or down.
sources.author: Sachin Malhotra
sources.work: How Claude Tag serves as Anthropic’s first responder for CI/CD failures

title.en: Named owner of an agent thread

definition.en: A team rule in which every line of agent work has a named person who owns it, and the agent shows user-visible changes to that person with before-and-after screenshots or recordings. [1]
definition.ru: Командное правило, при котором у каждой линии работы агента есть названный ответственный человек, и агент показывает ему видимые пользователю изменения со скриншотами или записями до и после. [1]

sources.quote: Every thread had a named human owner, and Claude highlighted any user-perceptible change with before-and-after screenshots or recordings for them to rule on.
sources.author: Raymond Wang, Sam Attard, and Issac G.
sources.work: How we made claude.ai 3x faster in two weeks

definition.en: The practice in which each task for the agent is written as a self-contained ticket stating what is wrong, what done looks like and which command proves it. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой каждая задача для агента записывается как самодостаточный тикет: что не так, как выглядит готовность и какая команда это доказывает. [1][2]

sources.quote: Write each task as a self-contained ticket that states what's wrong, what done looks like, and how to prove it.
sources.author: Addy Osmani
sources.work: Claude Code in the cloud: a field guide to cloud sessions

sources.quote: Ask for evidence. Name the command that proves the task is done, and read Claude's summary before the diff.
sources.author: Addy Osmani
sources.work: Claude Code in the cloud: a field guide to cloud sessions

definition.en: A prompting habit in which the agent is told to take more risks and try more ambitious ideas. [1][2]
definition.ru: Приём промптинга, при котором агенту говорят больше рисковать и пробовать более амбициозные идеи. [1][2]

sources.quote: A lot of what we did, especially early on, was to encourage Claude to be bolder.
sources.author: Raymond Wang, Sam Attard, and Issac G.
sources.work: How we made claude.ai 3x faster in two weeks

sources.quote: Encourage the model to take more risks and try ambitious ideas. You will not believe it but this worked.
sources.author: sankalp
sources.work: Auto-research with codex: How I achieved a 232x Faster Kernel over baseline with Codex in GPU Mode's qr_v2 problem

definition.en: The practice in which agent instructions, in a skill or the project instruction file, keep a section of gotchas built from the failure points the agent actually hit, updated over time. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой инструкции агента, в скилле или в файле инструкций проекта, содержат раздел подвохов, собранный из реальных мест, где агент ошибался, и пополняемый со временем. [1][2]

sources.quote: These sections should be built up from common failure points that Claude runs into when using your skill. Ideally, you will update your skill over time to capture these gotchas.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar
sources.work: Lessons from building Claude Code: How we use skills

sources.quote: Keep your CLAUDE.md lightweight and briefly describe what your repo is for, but spend most of the tokens on gotchas inside of the codebase.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar
sources.work: The new rules of context engineering for Claude 5 generation models

definition.en: The practice in which agent context is split into a tree of files, and the agent is told which files exist so that it reads each one only when it becomes relevant. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой контекст агента разбит на дерево файлов, и агенту сообщают, какие файлы есть, чтобы он читал каждый только тогда, когда он становится нужен. [1][2]

sources.quote: Instead, consider having a tree of files that can be loaded at the right time.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar
sources.work: The new rules of context engineering for Claude 5 generation models

sources.quote: Tell Claude what files are in your skill, and it will read them at appropriate times.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar
sources.work: Lessons from building Claude Code: How we use skills

definition.en: The practice in which constraints added to agent instructions for earlier, weaker models are reviewed and deleted, leaving the agent to rely on context and judgement. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой ограничения, добавленные в инструкции агента ради прежних, более слабых моделей, пересматривают и удаляют, оставляя агенту опираться на контекст и суждение. [1]

sources.quote: And while these constraints were once needed to avoid worst case scenarios, we have since found we can delete many of them and let the model use surrounding context and judgement instead.
sources.author: Thariq Shihipar
sources.work: The new rules of context engineering for Claude 5 generation models

definition.en: The practice in which a person who wants to understand part of a codebase asks the agent to write an explainer for exactly that part. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой человек, желающий понять часть кодовой базы, просит агента написать объяснение именно этой части. [1]

sources.quote: When someone wants to understand a part of the codebase, they ask Claude to write an explainer for exactly that slice.
sources.author: Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang
sources.work: How the Claude Code team does code review

definition.en: The practice in which verbose reading such as file search, logs and test output goes to subagents on a smaller model, while code edits and decisions stay on the main model. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой объёмное чтение, например поиск файлов, логи и вывод тестов, отдаётся субагентам на младшей модели, а правки кода и решения остаются на основной модели. [1][2]

sources.quote: Keep small models on work where a mistake is cheap to spot, like finding files, running tests and reading logs. Keep code edits and judgment calls on the main model.
sources.author: Addy Osmani
sources.work: Which Claude model should you build with? Fable, Opus, Sonnet, or Haiku

sources.quote: Keep the expensive model's context for the decisions, and let cheaper subagents do the verbose reading.
sources.author: Addy Osmani
sources.work: Which Claude model should you build with? Fable, Opus, Sonnet, or Haiku

definition.en: The practice in which the agent is connected to the team's own production traces and asked to find issues on hot code paths, and each resulting pull request links an example trace that shows the extra query or call. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агента подключают к трейсам продакшена самой команды и просят найти проблемы на горячих участках кода, а каждый итоговый пул-реквест ссылается на пример трейса с лишним запросом или вызовом. [1][2]

sources.quote: For the last few weeks I’ve used a coding agent to find and fix backend performance issues in Sentry, starting from the traces Sentry sends to itself.
sources.author: Scott Cooper
sources.work: Finding backend performance wins with a coding agent

sources.quote: Every PR links an example trace showing the extra query or call, so that it's a bit easier for a reviewer to understand.
sources.author: Scott Cooper
sources.work: Finding backend performance wins with a coding agent

title.ru: База только для чтения для агента

definition.en: The practice in which the agent has access to a read-only copy of the database and validates its query changes there instead of guessing their effect. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой у агента есть доступ к копии базы данных только для чтения, и он проверяет на ней свои изменения запросов, а не угадывает их эффект. [1]

sources.quote: Making sure the agent has the ability to validate changes in the read-only database rather than guessing leads to much better results.
sources.author: Scott Cooper
sources.work: Finding backend performance wins with a coding agent

title.ru: Запись бага до и после исправления

definition.en: The practice in which, for a bug fix, the agent reproduces the issue, records the broken behavior, implements the fix and repeats the same steps to show the before and after; the team keeps the instructions for this in a skill. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой для исправления бага агент воспроизводит проблему, записывает сломанное поведение, вносит исправление и повторяет те же шаги, чтобы показать «до» и «после»; инструкции для этого команда держит в скилле. [1][2]

sources.quote: For bug fixes, River can reproduce the issue, record the broken behavior, implement the fix, and then repeat the same steps to show the before and after.
sources.author: Michael Garfinkle, Mauricio de Meirelles, David Cortes
sources.work: We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment (2026)

sources.quote: So we created a skill to teach agents how to test their changes and prove their work.
sources.author: Michael Garfinkle, Mauricio de Meirelles, David Cortes
sources.work: We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment (2026)

definition.en: The practice in which a team keeps a pool of prepared machines for agents, with the main branch checked out, tools installed, apps built and caches warm, so that an agent claims one instead of waiting for setup. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой команда держит пул подготовленных машин для агентов: основная ветка выкачана, инструменты установлены, приложения собраны, кэши прогреты, и агент берёт готовую машину вместо ожидания настройки. [1][2]

sources.quote: So, instead of preparing a Mac after a request arrives, we switched to keeping a pool of warm Macs at the ready: main checked out (no small feat, as our monorepo is massive), tools installed, apps built, and caches warm.
sources.author: Michael Garfinkle, Mauricio de Meirelles, David Cortes
sources.work: We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment (2026)

sources.quote: Devboxes are pre-warmed so one can be spun up in 10 seconds, with Stripe code and services pre-loaded.
sources.author: Alistair Gray
sources.work: Minions: Stripe’s one-shot, end-to-end coding agents

definition.en: The practice in which long-running tasks are started in terminal panes, such as tmux panes, that the agent observes in real time, instead of the agent sleeping or setting timeouts while it waits. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой долгие задачи запускаются в панелях терминала, например tmux, за которыми агент следит в реальном времени, вместо того чтобы засыпать или ставить таймауты в ожидании. [1]

sources.quote: And instead of sleeping or setting timeouts for the Mac to finish long-running tasks, we used tmux panes that River could observe in real time.
sources.author: Michael Garfinkle, Mauricio de Meirelles, David Cortes
sources.work: We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment (2026)

definition.en: The practice in which every fact the agent extracts from legacy code carries a file:line reference back to that code. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой каждый факт, извлечённый агентом из унаследованного кода, несёт ссылку file:line на этот код. [1]

sources.quote: Source traceability is the real anti-hallucination mechanism. Every extracted fact carries a file:line reference back to the legacy code.
sources.author: Shashank Mishra
sources.work: AI-assisted migration: Critical lessons from the modernization frontlines

definition.en: The practice in which every fact the agent extracts from legacy code carries a green, amber or red confidence marker, and ambiguous code is flagged in the output so that a human expert resolves it. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой каждый факт, извлечённый агентом из унаследованного кода, несёт зелёную, жёлтую или красную метку уверенности, а неоднозначный код отмечается в выводе, чтобы его разрешил эксперт. [1][2]

sources.quote: To achieve this, every extracted fact carried a green, amber or red confidence marker.
sources.author: Shashank Mishra
sources.work: AI-assisted migration: Critical lessons from the modernization frontlines

sources.quote: One was that if the code was ambiguous, the AI had to flag the ambiguity in its output so a human expert could resolve it.
sources.author: Shashank Mishra
sources.work: AI-assisted migration: Critical lessons from the modernization frontlines

definition.en: The practice in which a team meets at regular intervals to examine what went well, what caused difficulty and what to change in how it works. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой команда регулярно собирается и разбирает, что прошло хорошо, что вызвало трудности и что изменить в своей работе. [1]

firstAppeared.note: Earliest found: Norman L. Kerth, Project Retrospectives: A Handbook for Team Reviews, Dorset House, 2001 (publisher page: https://dorsethouse.com/books/pr.html); the practice is older

sources.quote: Team retrospectives examine what went well, what caused difficulty, and what to improve. Session logs give us a detailed record for a similar process around our agents.
sources.author: Ron Meldiner
sources.work: How to use AI session logs to improve coding agent workflows

definition.en: The practice in which a team writes down each significant architectural decision as a short record kept with the code. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой команда записывает каждое значимое архитектурное решение короткой записью, которая хранится рядом с кодом. [1]

firstAppeared.note: year stated on the source page

sources.quote: The point of an ADR was always to stop the next person from undoing a decision they didn’t know about. The next person is now, more often than not, an agent.
sources.author: Edy Silva
sources.work: Stale docs are prompt injection you wrote yourself - The Miners

origin.en: Proposed by Michael Nygard in 2011 (per Edy Silva, Codeminer42).
origin.ru: Предложены Майклом Найгардом в 2011 году (по Эди Силве, Codeminer42).

definition.en: The practice in which several independent teams implement the same specification, the versions run in parallel, and a voting rule masks the faults of a single version. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой несколько независимых команд реализуют одну спецификацию, версии работают параллельно, и правило голосования скрывает ошибки отдельной версии. [1]

firstAppeared.note: year stated on the source page

sources.quote: This paper revisits the classical N-Version Programming literature in the modern agentic setting. We design and perform a reproduction of the original Knight–Leveson experiment with AI coding agents.
sources.author: Javier Ron, Benoit Baudry, Martin Monperrus
sources.work: N-Version Programming with Coding Agents

origin.en: Proposed by Liming Chen and Algirdas Avizienis in 1978 (per Ron, Baudry and Monperrus).
origin.ru: Предложено Лимином Чэнем и Альгирдасом Авиженисом в 1978 году (по Рону, Бодри и Монперрюсу).

definition.en: The practice in which a developer first builds a small end-to-end slice of functionality that touches all layers of the system, then grows the system from that working slice. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик сначала строит небольшой сквозной срез функциональности через все слои системы, а затем наращивает систему от этого работающего среза. [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: year stated on the source page

sources.quote: The concept of a tracer bullet comes from The Pragmatic Programmer. It's a small, end-to-end slice of functionality that touches all the layers of your system at once.
sources.author: Matt Pocock
sources.work: Tracer Bullets: Keeping AI Slop Under Control

sources.quote: Central to tracer bullet development is the idea of a skeleton application, in which one thin line of execution goes end to end.
sources.author: Andy Hunt and Dave Thomas
sources.work: Tracer Bullets and Prototypes

origin.en: From The Pragmatic Programmer (per Matt Pocock).
origin.ru: Из книги The Pragmatic Programmer (по Мэтту Пококу).

definition.en: The practice in which deliberate faults are introduced into the code to check whether the tests detect them. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой в код намеренно вносят ошибки, чтобы проверить, обнаруживают ли их тесты. [1]

sources.quote: Mutation testing is an old technique. What's interesting here is that the AI can create more realistic, plausible mutations, much cheaper (in time, money, tears, and sweat) than a human developer.
sources.author: Senko Rašić
sources.work: Improving AI-generated tests using mutation testing

definition.en: The practice in which the reviewer sits with the author of a change, and the author talks through its intent and structure. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой ревьюер садится рядом с автором изменения, и автор рассказывает о его замысле и устройстве. [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: year stated on the source page

sources.quote: Now, with agents producing code at a pace that makes every PR feel like one of those massive ones, the approach I used — sitting down and talking it through — clearly can't happen for every change. But the principle behind it can.
sources.author: Chris Hughes
sources.work: Pull Requests Were Never Really About the Code

sources.quote: A structured walk-through is a review of a developer's work (program design, code, documentation, etc.) by fellow project members invited by the developer.
sources.author: IBM
sources.work: Improved Programming Technologies: An Overview

origin.en: Described as the «structured walk-through» in an IBM overview of programming technologies (earliest source found)
origin.ru: Описан как «structured walk-through» в обзоре IBM о технологиях программирования (самый ранний найденный источник)

definition.en: The practice in which a team enforces code style and safeguards through formatters, linters and pre-commit or CI checks instead of writing them as rules in documentation. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой команда закрепляет стиль кода и защитные правила через форматтеры, линтеры и проверки перед коммитом или в CI, а не описывает их в документации. [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: year stated on the source page

sources.quote: Code style rules, in particular, should live in a formatter or linter rather than in docs. The same rule applies to LLM safeguards: it’s better to move a rule into a formatter config or a custom linter rule than to add it to AGENTS.md.
sources.author: Andrey Sitnik and Travis Turner
sources.work: Stop writing rules in AGENTS.md: use agent hooks and nano-staged instead

sources.quote: Lint is a command which examines C source programs, detecting a number of bugs and obscurities.
sources.author: S. C. Johnson
sources.work: Lint, a C Program Checker

origin.en: The checker lint was described by S. C. Johnson at Bell Laboratories
origin.ru: Программу проверки lint описал С. Джонсон в Bell Laboratories

definition.en: The practice in which a change is released behind a switch that turns it on for some users or for all, without a new release. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой изменение выпускают за переключателем, который включает его для части пользователей или для всех без нового релиза. [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: year stated on the source page

sources.quote: AI changes ride behind flags the same way risky human changes always have.
sources.author: Liz Fong-Jones
sources.work: AI Amplifies Your Existing Practices: Lessons from Our Shift to an AI-First Strategy

sources.quote: Flags allow us to restrict features to certain environments, while still using the same code base on all servers.
sources.author: Ross Harmes
sources.work: Flipping Out

origin.en: Described by Ross Harmes on the Flickr engineering blog (earliest source found)
origin.ru: Описаны Россом Хармсом в инженерном блоге Flickr (самый ранний найденный источник)

title.en: First investigation of an alert by an agent

definition.en: The practice in which an agent does the first investigation of a production alert: reads the logs, metrics and code, reports a root cause with its evidence, and leaves any change to production to a person's approval. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой первое расследование алерта в продакшене делает агент: читает логи, метрики и код, сообщает первопричину с доказательствами, а любое изменение в продакшене оставляет на одобрение человеку. [1][2]

sources.quote: The agent does the first investigation for our backend team. It reads the same logs, databases, metrics and code an engineer would, posts a root cause with its evidence in Slack, and waits for a person to approve anything that would change production.
sources.author: Aditya Nugraha
sources.work: How We Built an AI Agent to Investigate Production Issues

sources.quote: Claude Tag kicks off a dynamic workflow with an orchestration agent that spins up executor subagents to investigate each dependency and source of truth.
sources.author: Sachin Malhotra
sources.work: How Claude Tag serves as Anthropic’s first responder for CI/CD failures

definition.en: The practice in which an alert passes through a chain of agents: one investigates and writes a plan, a second reviews the plan, and a third opens a pull request with a scoped fix for the on-call engineer. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой алерт проходит через цепочку агентов: один расследует и пишет план, второй проверяет план, третий открывает pull request с ограниченным исправлением для дежурного инженера. [1]

sources.quote: An alert lands, it gets investigated, a plan gets written, another agent reviews that plan, and if it holds up, a scoped fix shows up as a PR with the on-call already tagged.
sources.author: Ari Salem
sources.work: Stories from the Factory Floor: Building a self-driving ops triage loop

definition.en: The practice in which the expected behaviour of a change is written down as structured acceptance criteria (given, when, then) before the code. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой ожидаемое поведение изменения записывают до кода в виде структурированных критериев приёмки (given, when, then). [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: Dan North, «Introducing BDD»: «This article first appeared in Better Software magazine in March 2006»

origin.en: Introduced by Dan North in «Introducing BDD», Better Software, March 2006
origin.ru: Предложена Дэном Нортом в статье «Introducing BDD», Better Software, март 2006

sources.quote: Give your AI agent BDD-style acceptance criteria, and it will have everything it needs to ensure the changes it makes will satisfy the expectations of what was originally intended.
sources.author: Yves Da Silva
sources.work: Set Your AI Up for Success: How BDD Tickets Drive Quality Outcomes

sources.quote: My response is behaviour-driven development (BDD).
sources.author: Dan North
sources.work: Introducing BDD

definition.en: The practice in which the depth of review for a change depends on its risk: a low-risk change gets a light check or merges automatically, everything else gets full review, and some kinds of code are kept out of automated review. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой глубина ревью изменения зависит от его риска: изменение с низким риском проходит лёгкую проверку или сливается автоматически, остальные проходят полное ревью, а часть кода исключена из автоматического ревью. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: Review depth is routed automatically: a trivial low-risk slice gets a one-reviewer scan, everything else gets a three-reviewer quorum, and code pull requests never skip deep review.
sources.author: Jonathan Wage
sources.work: Risk-Proportional Review for AI Agents

sources.quote: We’re learning where to apply human judgment — auto-merging what’s safe, focusing review where it matters most — and rethinking how we plan and prioritize as the bottleneck moves from coding to decision-making.
sources.author: Spotify Engineering
sources.work: Coding Is No Longer the Constraint: Scaling Developer Experience to Teams and Agents at Spotify

sources.quote: Diffs that touch open-source code, SOX-scoped code, or code requiring additional reviews are excluded. These exclusions protect areas where constraints require human judgment.
sources.author: Chris Adams et al.
sources.work: Automating Low-Risk Code Review at Meta: RADAR, Risk Calibration, and Review Efficiency

title.en: CI workflow files as high risk
title.ru: Файлы CI как зона высокого риска

definition.en: The practice in which the files that define the CI pipeline are treated as high risk, because an agent that can edit the pipeline can weaken the review of its own work. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой файлы, задающие конвейер CI, считаются зоной высокого риска: агент, который может править конвейер, может ослабить проверку собственной работы. [1]

sources.quote: One rule matters for agents: the files defining our CI workflows are high risk, because an agent that can edit the pipeline enforcing its own review can weaken it.
sources.author: Jonathan Wage
sources.work: Risk-Proportional Review for AI Agents

title.en: Track record before landing without review
title.ru: Чистая история до слияния без ревью

definition.en: The practice in which an automated workflow may land changes without review of each one only after a clean record over a set period: no incidents, few reverts, few rejections by people and enough landed changes. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой автоматический процесс получает право сливать изменения без ревью каждого из них только после чистой истории за заданный срок: без инцидентов, с малым числом откатов и отклонений людьми и с достаточным числом слитых изменений. [1]

sources.quote: Risk history heuristics. Each runbook must demonstrate a clean track record over a 60-day lookback window: zero PIs, a low revert rate, a low human rejection rate, and a minimum number of landed diffs to establish statistical confidence.
sources.author: Chris Adams et al.
sources.work: Automating Low-Risk Code Review at Meta: RADAR, Risk Calibration, and Review Efficiency

title.en: Cap on CI rounds per agent run
title.ru: Предел прогонов CI на один запуск агента

definition.en: The practice in which an unattended agent gets at most a fixed number of CI rounds per task, two in the source, because every round costs tokens, compute and time. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент без присмотра получает не больше заданного числа прогонов CI на задачу, в источнике двух, потому что каждый прогон стоит токенов, вычислений и времени. [1]

sources.quote: Since CI runs cost tokens, compute, and time, we only have at most two rounds of CI.
sources.author: Alistair Gray
sources.work: Minions: Stripe’s one-shot, end-to-end coding agents

definition.en: The practice in which code generated for a one-off task is run and thrown away without being read. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой код, сгенерированный для разовой задачи, запускают и выбрасывают, не читая. [1]

sources.quote: It's a throwaway artifact. Run it, get your answer, move on. I am usually not even going to look at the code that was generated; I certainly don’t care how it is structured.
sources.author: Oren Eini
sources.work: Using AI agents in long-lived software projects

title.ru: Аудит кодовой базы вместе с агентом

definition.en: The practice in which the developer asks the agent to audit the codebase for one named problem and talks the findings through with it until a concrete change is clear. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик просит агента проверить кодовую базу на одну названную проблему и обсуждает с ним находки, пока не станет ясно конкретное изменение. [1]

sources.quote: I’ll start a conversation by saying “Let’s audit this codebase for unreachable code,” or “This function makes my eyes bleed,” and we’ll have a conversation about it until something actionable comes up.
sources.author: Bram Cohen
sources.work: The Cult Of Vibe Coding Is Insane

definition.en: The practice in which the agent shows its proposed code in the chat and the developer types every edit into the project by hand. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент показывает предложенный код в чате, а разработчик сам вносит каждую правку в проект вручную. [1]

sources.quote: I ask my coding assistant to generate code in the chat, then manually make all the edits myself.
sources.author: Ankur Sethi
sources.work: Prevent cognitive debt by manually retyping LLM-generated code

definition.en: The practice in which the developer sets a ceiling on the number of agent threads run at once, three to four in the source, depending on their complexity. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик задаёт потолок числа одновременно идущих потоков агентов, в источнике три-четыре, в зависимости от их сложности. [1]

sources.quote: My ceiling for a typical session is somewhere around three to four threads depending on complexity.
sources.author: Addy Osmani
sources.work: Your parallel Agent limit

title.en: Agent session transcripts in the take-home
title.ru: Записи сессий с агентом в тестовом задании

definition.en: The practice in which a candidate submits the transcripts of their sessions with the agent as part of the take-home, next to the code and the demo. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой кандидат сдаёт записи своих сессий с агентом как часть тестового задания, вместе с кодом и демонстрацией. [1]

sources.quote: AI transcripts went from not existing to being the second deliverable, right between the code and the demo.
sources.author: Quentin Rousseau
sources.work: Re-thinking candidate take-homes in the AI era: transcripts over code

title.en: Take-home built for work with agents
title.ru: Тестовое задание, рассчитанное на работу с агентом

definition.en: The practice in which a take-home allows agents and is built around a longer problem that an agent does not solve whole, with starter code that leaves the tooling to the candidate. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой тестовое задание разрешает агентов и построено вокруг длинной задачи, которую агент не решает целиком, а стартовый код оставляет инструменты на кандидата. [1][2]

sources.quote: For this take-home, we explicitly indicate otherwise. Longer-horizon problems are harder for AI to solve completely, so candidates can use AI tools (as they would on the job) while still needing to demonstrate their own skills.
sources.author: Tristan Hume
sources.work: Designing AI resistant technical evaluations

sources.quote: Unlike Zachtronics games, I intentionally provided no visualization or debugging tools. The starter code only checks whether solutions are valid.
sources.author: Tristan Hume
sources.work: Designing AI resistant technical evaluations
